title: Packages
text: Open R data packages I develop for transport and urban research. Each one has its own documentation site with examples.

title: Packages
text:
ActiveCA
Analysis-ready Canadian time-use data on walking and cycling. ActiveCA provides active travel episodes from seven cycles of the General Social Survey - Time Use (1986 - 2022), with origin and destination types, trip durations, province, urban/rural setting and episode weights, plus pre-estimated impedance functions for walking and cycling in Census Metropolitan Areas and Census Agglomerations.
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("dias-bruno/ActiveCA")
Documentation GitHub Paper (EPB, 2025)

title: Packages
text:
CommuteCA
Datasets and standardized methods for job accessibility analysis with Canada’s 2021 Census of Population. CommuteCA includes calibrated impedance functions for walking, cycling, public transit and car (optionally by education level) at the Census Division, CMA/CA and provincial levels; census tract data on labour force by commuting mode and jobs; functions to look up impedance functions and compute impedance from travel times; and R Markdown templates for accessibility modelling and assessment, including Hansen-type and spatial availability measures.
install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("dias-bruno/CommuteCA")
Documentation GitHub

title: Packages
text:
amazonULC
Urban land cover classification maps for Brazilian Amazonian cities: Altamira, Cametá, Marabá, Santarém and part of the Belém Metropolitan Area, all in Pará. Classes include vegetation, water, exposed ground, roofing materials (ceramic, fibre cement, high-gloss) and paved and unpaved roads.
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("dias-bruno/amazonULC")
Documentation GitHub

title: Bruno Dias dos Santos
text:
I am a PhD candidate in (Transportation) Geography at McMaster University (Hamilton, ON, Canada), in the final year of my program, with my defence planned for summer 2027. My research uses spatial and statistical models to study transportation equity, particularly how access to jobs and opportunities is distributed across places and population groups in Canada, and to support more equitable transportation planning and policy. My educational background is in Environmental and Urban Engineering (UFABC, Brazil) and Remote Sensing (INPE, Brazil / McMaster University, Canada).
I work with Canadian survey microdata - the Census and the General Social Survey, through the Statistics Canada Research Data Centre, and the National Survey on Transport Poverty, and I build open tools for this research, including the R packages ActiveCA, CommuteCA and amazonULC. Before coming to Canada, I used remote sensing and machine learning to map urban and socio-environmental patterns in Brazilian Amazonian cities and precarious settlements in São Paulo.
Outside research, I teach spatial statistics and GIS at McMaster, facilitate the MePLUS science program for high school students from equity-deserving groups, and help run the Latin American Network at McMaster University.

title: Research
text: My doctoral research, Developing standards for equity in transportation planning and policy, combines accessibility analysis, survey microdata and statistical modelling to ask how much access to opportunities is considered sufficient, and for whom. Earlier, my work used remote sensing and machine learning to map urban and socio-environmental patterns in Brazilian Amazonian cities and precarious settlements in São Paulo, Brazil.
